text: Toto checks a California total-loss valuation against 10 CCR section 2695.8, compares the vehicle with market listings, drafts an evidence-backed counteroffer, estimates net payout, and helps shortlist replacement vehicles. Toto provides information and estimates, not legal advice or a guarantee that an insurer will change its offer.
Check 1: Toto compares each insurer comparable's make and model with the loss vehicle. A mismatch is flagged for review under Toto's reading of 10 CCR section 2695.8(b)(2).

Check 2: Toto flags an insurer comparable with an older model year than the loss vehicle. Newer model years may be acceptable when same-year matches are scarce. This is an automated screening check, not a legal conclusion.

Check 3: Toto checks whether a comparable is local and recent. The app uses a 100-mile radius and a 90-day listing-age threshold as its own screening settings for 10 CCR section 2695.8(b)(2) and (b)(4)(A). Missing distance or date is marked unknown rather than assumed to pass.
Check 4: Toto checks whether each comparable is identified by a VIN, stock number, or plate and includes seller contact information, as part of its screening under 10 CCR section 2695.8(b)(2).

Check 5: Toto compares trim, options, and odometer readings. Its screening flags mileage differences greater than 20 percent and missing options; that 20 percent threshold is an app setting, not a quoted legal threshold.

Check 6: Toto flags comparable adjustments that are unlabeled or grouped under vague labels such as other or miscellaneous. The report should make adjustments understandable and itemized under the app's reading of 10 CCR section 2695.8(b)(2).

Check 7: Toto flags a condition deduction when the report does not document a below-average condition. The report's condition grade and supporting inspection notes or photos matter; the app does not make a final legal determination.
Check 8: Toto recalculates the average of adjusted comparable values and compares it with the report's base value, screening the calculation under 10 CCR section 2695.8(b)(4)(A).

Check 9: Toto checks whether the offer total reconciles with base value, condition adjustment, sales tax, title and transfer fees, prorated registration, and deductible. It flags missing line items and arithmetic differences under 10 CCR section 2695.8(b)(1).
Check 10: Toto flags when the report does not include a written explanation of how the total-loss value was determined, under the app's screening of 10 CCR section 2695.8(b)(4).

A market value and counteroffer from Toto are estimates. The app uses comparable listings and deterministic code for dollar calculations. Listings may be stale or imperfect matches, and an insurer may disagree.

Toto displays a 35-day date based on the offer date as a reminder related to 10 CCR section 2695.8(c). The insurer may have an exception in some cases. The displayed date is not individualized legal advice; users should confirm deadlines with the insurer or a qualified professional.

Net payout is estimated by subtracting an auto-loan balance from a settlement amount. A negative result means the estimated loan balance exceeds that settlement. GAP coverage may help with a shortfall, but coverage and actual amounts must be confirmed with the lender or insurer.
A prequalification amount and APR shown by Toto are illustrative estimates from a test profile or connected sandbox. They are not a credit decision, commitment to lend, or lender offer.

The replacement-car deposit in this Toto demo is a test-mode checkout that accepts only Visa test card numbers. No payment is made and no card is charged. Before any deposit, the owner grants a mandate with a budget, a spending cap, the sellers that passed the CRS check and a 48-hour expiry. The deposit stays locked until the seller check comes back clean.

The user reviews and approves the counteroffer letter and any simulated hold. The voice assistant can explain the claim and evidence but must not submit a letter, select a car, place a hold, or take another action for the user.
